# NOTE: imputeTS was a leftover import from the old Stineman-interpolation
# preprocessing pipeline (see README) and is not called anywhere in this
# file or in util.R (which does its own gap-aware cleaning). Dropped so
# the app does not require an extra, unused dependency to start.
tryCatch({
  source("util.R")
  sql_db_file <<- "exoplanet_db.sqlite"
  processed <<- list.files("trained_models/", full.names = F)
  all_stars <<- list.files("data/", pattern = ".tbl", full.names = F)
  data_dir <<- "data/"
  plots_dir <<- "plots/test_pred_plot/"
}, error = function(e) {
  source("../util.R")
  sql_db_file <<- "../exoplanet_db.sqlite"
  processed <<- list.files("../trained_models/", full.names = F)
  all_stars <<- list.files("../data/", pattern = ".tbl", full.names = F)
  data_dir <<- "../data/"
  plots_dir <<- "../plots/test_pred_plot/"
})

return_stars <- function(processed) {
  processed <- strsplit(processed, "_")
  processed <- unique(sapply(processed, function(filename) filename[1]))
  return(processed)
}

# Converts a {starts, ends} list (as returned by get_candidate_indices) into
# a list of c(start, end) windows, dropping the (0, 0) placeholder row used
# to mark "no tags yet".
indices_to_windows <- function(idx) {
  if (is.null(idx) || length(idx$starts) == 0) return(list())
  keep <- which(idx$starts > 0 & idx$ends >= idx$starts)
  if (length(keep) == 0) return(list())
  lapply(keep, function(k) c(idx$starts[k], idx$ends[k]))
}

# Builds the interactive light-curve plot.
#   mode = "view" -> read-only, points colored red/black by idx_mask (the
#                     usual model-detection / saved-tag overlay)
#   mode = "tag"  -> manual tagging session: draws each window in
#                     tag_windows_list as a translucent, EDITABLE rectangle
#                     that the user can drag on either edge to resize, or
#                     drag the body to move. New windows are defined by
#                     drag-selecting empty plot area (dragmode = "select"),
#                     which is a distinct gesture from editing an existing
#                     shape, so both work on the same plot at once.
# Label -> fill / border colour for transit-window shapes.
# Tag mode shapes are editable; view-mode shapes are shaded but static.
lc_label_colors <- list(
  "Transit"    = list(fill = "rgba(255,165,0,0.25)",   border = "rgba(217,119,6,0.90)"),
  "Sinusoidal" = list(fill = "rgba(139,92,246,0.25)",  border = "rgba(109,40,217,0.90)"),
  "Flare"      = list(fill = "rgba(239,68,68,0.25)",   border = "rgba(185,28,28,0.90)"),
  "Odd-Even"   = list(fill = "rgba(20,184,166,0.25)",  border = "rgba(13,148,136,0.90)"),
  "Uncertain"  = list(fill = "rgba(156,163,175,0.25)", border = "rgba(107,114,128,0.90)")
)
lc_get_col <- function(lbl) {
  if (is.null(lbl) || !nzchar(as.character(lbl)) || !lbl %in% names(lc_label_colors))
    lc_label_colors[["Transit"]]
  else
    lc_label_colors[[lbl]]
}

# Builds the interactive light-curve plot.
#   mode = "view" -> read-only; saved windows shown as non-editable shaded regions;
#                    candidate points coloured red via idx_mask.
#   mode = "tag"  -> tagging session: windows are editable, colour-coded by label.
# The x-axis is always in elapsed days (cadence index converted via cadence_days);
# xlim is still supplied in cadence-index units and converted internally so
# that all zoom state remains in the same units as the DB.
build_light_curve_plotly <- function(test_vec, pred_vec, xlim, ylim, idx_mask,
                                      title_str, mode = c("view", "tag"),
                                      tag_windows_list = NULL, tag_labels_list = NULL,
                                      source_id = "trainPlot_src",
                                      cadence_days = 29.4 / 1440) {
  mode <- match.arg(mode)
  n <- length(test_vec)
  x_days <- (seq_len(n) - 1L) * cadence_days   # elapsed days for the x-axis
  marker_color <- if (mode == "tag") rep("black", n) else ifelse(idx_mask, "red", "black")

  p <- plot_ly(source = source_id) %>%
    add_markers(x = x_days, y = test_vec,
                marker = list(color = marker_color, size = 4),
                name = "Light Curve", hoverinfo = "x+y")

  if (length(pred_vec) == n) {
    p <- p %>% add_lines(x = x_days, y = pred_vec,
                          line = list(color = "dodgerblue", width = 1.5),
                          name = "Autoencoder Baseline")
  }

  # Draw window shapes (editable in tag mode, static in view mode)
  shapes_list <- list()
  if (length(tag_windows_list) > 0) {
    for (i in seq_along(tag_windows_list)) {
      w   <- tag_windows_list[[i]]
      lbl <- if (!is.null(tag_labels_list) && i <= length(tag_labels_list)) tag_labels_list[[i]] else "Transit"
      col <- lc_get_col(lbl)
      shapes_list[[length(shapes_list) + 1]] <- list(
        type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper",
        x0 = (w[1] - 1L) * cadence_days, x1 = (w[2] - 1L) * cadence_days,
        y0 = 0, y1 = 1,
        fillcolor = col$fill,
        line = list(color = col$border, width = 2),
        editable = (mode == "tag")
      )
    }
  }

  # Convert xlim (cadence indices) to day-units for the plot axis range
  xlim_days <- if (!is.null(xlim)) (xlim - 1L) * cadence_days else NULL

  p <- p %>%
    layout(title = title_str,
           xaxis = list(title = "Time (days)", range = xlim_days),
           yaxis = list(title = "Normalized Flux", range = ylim),
           dragmode = "select",
           shapes = shapes_list,
           legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.15)) %>%
    config(displaylogo = FALSE,
           editable = (mode == "tag"),
           edits = list(shapePosition = (mode == "tag")))

  return(p)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# BLS (Box Least Squares) period verification
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# A self-contained, heuristic BLS-style search used only by the dashboard
# to sanity-check the period/duration/depth implied by a star's currently
# tagged (or model-detected) transit windows against the full light curve.
# This is NOT the training pipeline's detection step - it is read-only and
# purely for on-screen verification.
#
#   flux         - numeric vector of (cleaned) flux values, one per cadence
#   windows      - list of c(start, end) cadence-index pairs for the
#                  currently tagged/detected windows; used only to seed a
#                  sensible transit-duration search range
#   cadence_days - days per cadence (Kepler long cadence ~29.4 min)
#   n_periods    - number of trial periods to scan
#   n_bins       - number of phase bins used for folding
#
# Returns NULL if there isn't enough usable data, otherwise a list with
# period_days, duration_days, depth, depth_pct, snr, folded_phase,
# folded_flux and transit_phase_range (for the verification plot).
run_bls_search <- function(flux, windows, cadence_days = 29.4 / 1440,
                            n_periods = 200, n_bins = 80) {
  n <- length(flux)
  ok <- is.finite(flux)
  if (sum(ok) < 20) return(NULL)

  idx <- which(ok)
  fl <- flux[ok]
  baseline <- stats::median(fl)
  resid <- baseline - fl  # positive during a transit dip, whatever the flux baseline is

  # Duration hint (in cadences) from currently tagged/detected windows
  win_lens <- if (length(windows) > 0) sapply(windows, function(w) diff(w) + 1) else numeric(0)
  dur_guess <- if (length(win_lens) > 0) stats::median(win_lens) else max(3, round(0.02 * n))
  dur_candidates <- unique(pmax(2, round(dur_guess * c(0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2))))

  min_period <- max(dur_candidates) * 3
  max_period <- floor(n / 2)
  if (!is.finite(min_period) || max_period <= min_period) return(NULL)
  period_grid <- unique(round(seq(min_period, max_period, length.out = n_periods)))

  # Sum of v over a circular window of length k starting at every position
  circular_rolling_sum <- function(v, k) {
    m <- length(v)
    ext <- c(v, v[seq_len(k)])
    csum <- c(0, cumsum(ext))
    csum[(k + 1):(m + k)] - csum[1:m]
  }

  best <- list(sr = -Inf)
  for (P in period_grid) {
    phase <- ((idx - 1) %% P) / P
    bin <- pmin(n_bins, floor(phase * n_bins) + 1)

    y <- numeric(n_bins); cnt <- numeric(n_bins)
    agg_sum <- tapply(resid, bin, sum)
    agg_cnt <- tapply(resid, bin, length)
    y[as.integer(names(agg_sum))] <- agg_sum
    cnt[as.integer(names(agg_cnt))] <- agg_cnt
    if (sum(cnt) == 0) next
    w <- cnt / sum(cnt)

    d_bins_set <- unique(pmax(1, pmin(n_bins - 1, round(n_bins * dur_candidates / P))))
    for (d_bins in d_bins_set) {
      roll_y <- circular_rolling_sum(y, d_bins)
      roll_w <- circular_rolling_sum(w, d_bins)
      sr <- (roll_y ^ 2) / (roll_w * (1 - roll_w) + 1e-9)
      j <- which.max(sr)
      if (isTRUE(sr[j] > best$sr) && roll_w[j] > 0) {
        best <- list(sr = sr[j], period = P, d_bins = d_bins, phase_bin = j,
                     w_in = roll_w[j], y_in = roll_y[j])
      }
    }
  }

  if (!is.finite(best$sr) || best$sr <= 0 || is.null(best$period)) return(NULL)

  period_days <- best$period * cadence_days
  duration_days <- (best$d_bins / n_bins) * period_days
  depth <- best$y_in / (best$w_in * length(idx))  # mean in-transit residual, flux units
  depth_pct <- if (abs(baseline) > 1e-9) 100 * depth / abs(baseline) else NA

  raw_phase <- ((idx - 1) %% best$period) / best$period
  transit_center <- ((best$phase_bin - 1) + best$d_bins / 2) / n_bins
  shifted_phase <- (raw_phase - transit_center + 0.5) %% 1  # re-center transit at phase 0.5
  half_dur_frac <- (best$d_bins / n_bins) / 2

  list(
    period_days = period_days,
    duration_days = duration_days,
    depth = depth,
    depth_pct = depth_pct,
    snr = sqrt(max(best$sr, 0)),
    folded_phase = shifted_phase,
    folded_flux = fl,
    transit_phase_range = c(0.5 - half_dur_frac, 0.5 + half_dur_frac)
  )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# GPU-accelerated period search (optional) with automatic CPU fallback
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# run_bls_search() above is a pure-R implementation, good enough for an
# on-demand sanity check, but not fast: a full period/duration grid search
# over a whole light curve is exactly the kind of embarrassingly parallel
# workload GPUs excel at. cuvarbase (PyCUDA) implements a GPU Box Least
# Squares search and is used in published TESS planet-search work; on real
# hardware its "fast" mode processes a ~70k-point Kepler light curve in
# roughly a second versus ~30s on CPU. This wrapper calls it through
# reticulate when available and returns NULL otherwise, so
# run_bls_search_auto() below can fall back to the CPU implementation the
# same way the Keras model-loading fallback works elsewhere in this file -
# both BLS implementations return the same list() shape, so nothing
# downstream (build_phase_fold_plotly, bls_panel) needs to know which ran.
#
# IMPORTANT, read before relying on this: this path requires a real CUDA
# GPU, reticulate, and a Python environment with cuvarbase installed. Only
# the unavailable-dependency fallback (reticulate/cuvarbase missing ->
# cleanly returns NULL, run_bls_search_auto() falls through to the CPU
# path) has been exercised here - there is no CUDA hardware in this
# development environment to run the GPU code path itself against.
run_bls_search_gpu <- function(flux, windows, cadence_days = 29.4 / 1440, n_periods = 200) {
  if (!requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE)) return(NULL)
  if (!isTRUE(tryCatch(reticulate::py_module_available("cuvarbase"), error = function(e) FALSE))) return(NULL)
  
  ok <- is.finite(flux)
  if (sum(ok) < 20) return(NULL)
  idx <- which(ok)
  fl <- flux[ok]
  n <- length(flux)
  
  t <- (idx - 1) * cadence_days
  y <- fl
  noise <- stats::mad(fl, na.rm = TRUE)
  dy <- rep(if (is.finite(noise) && noise > 0) noise else 1e-3, length(fl))
  
  win_lens <- if (length(windows) > 0) sapply(windows, function(w) diff(w) + 1) else numeric(0)
  dur_guess <- if (length(win_lens) > 0) stats::median(win_lens) else max(3, round(0.02 * n))
  dur_candidates <- unique(pmax(2, round(dur_guess * c(0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2))))
  
  min_period_days <- max(dur_candidates) * 3 * cadence_days
  max_period_days <- floor(n / 2) * cadence_days
  if (!is.finite(min_period_days) || max_period_days <= min_period_days) return(NULL)
  
  fmin <- 1 / max_period_days
  fmax <- 1 / min_period_days
  freqs <- seq(fmin, fmax, length.out = n_periods)
  
  qmin <- max(0.001, min(dur_candidates) * cadence_days / max_period_days)
  qmax <- min(0.5, max(dur_candidates) * cadence_days / min_period_days)
  if (qmax <= qmin) qmax <- qmin * 1.5
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    cvb_bls <- reticulate::import("cuvarbase.bls")
    np <- reticulate::import("numpy")
    sol <- cvb_bls$eebls_gpu_fast(
      np$asarray(t), np$asarray(y), np$asarray(dy), np$asarray(freqs),
      qmin = qmin, qmax = qmax, dlogq = 0.1, noverlap = 3
    )
    list(bls_power = sol[[1]], sols = sol[[2]])
  }, error = function(e) e)
  
  if (inherits(result, "error") || is.null(result)) return(NULL)
  
  bls_power <- as.numeric(result$bls_power)
  best_i <- which.max(bls_power)
  if (length(best_i) == 0 || !is.finite(bls_power[best_i])) return(NULL)
  
  best_freq <- freqs[best_i]
  period_days <- 1 / best_freq
  q_best <- tryCatch(as.numeric(result$sols[[best_i]][[1]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  phi0_best <- tryCatch(as.numeric(result$sols[[best_i]][[2]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  if (!is.finite(q_best) || !is.finite(phi0_best) || q_best <= 0) return(NULL)
  
  duration_days <- q_best * period_days
  
  baseline <- stats::median(y)
  phase <- ((t / period_days) - phi0_best) %% 1
  in_transit <- phase < q_best
  if (sum(in_transit) < 2) return(NULL)
  depth <- baseline - mean(y[in_transit])
  depth_pct <- if (abs(baseline) > 1e-9) 100 * depth / abs(baseline) else NA
  out_sd <- stats::sd(y[!in_transit])
  snr <- if (is.finite(out_sd) && out_sd > 0) abs(depth) / (out_sd / sqrt(sum(in_transit))) else NA
  
  shifted_phase <- (phase - q_best / 2 + 0.5) %% 1
  half_dur_frac <- q_best / 2
  
  list(
    period_days = period_days,
    duration_days = duration_days,
    depth = depth,
    depth_pct = depth_pct,
    snr = snr,
    folded_phase = shifted_phase,
    folded_flux = y,
    transit_phase_range = c(0.5 - half_dur_frac, 0.5 + half_dur_frac)
  )
}

# Tries the GPU path first, falling back to the pure-R CPU implementation on
# any missing dependency or runtime error. Tags the result with $engine so
# the UI can show which one actually ran.
run_bls_search_auto <- function(flux, windows, cadence_days = 29.4 / 1440) {
  gpu_res <- tryCatch(run_bls_search_gpu(flux, windows, cadence_days), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(gpu_res)) {
    gpu_res$engine <- "gpu"
    return(gpu_res)
  }
  cpu_res <- run_bls_search(flux, windows, cadence_days)
  if (!is.null(cpu_res)) cpu_res$engine <- "cpu"
  cpu_res
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Statistical vetting checks (odd-even transit test, secondary eclipse)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two classic, purely statistical checks used as vetting features in
# published exoplanet-candidate classifiers (e.g. ExoMiner's odd-even and
# secondary-eclipse diagnostic branches, NotPlaNET's contaminant CNN): a
# genuine planet should transit with equal depth at every epoch and show no
# significant secondary eclipse opposite the primary. A significant
# difference in either is the classic signature of a background/blended
# eclipsing binary rather than a real planet. These need no trained model
# and no labeled data - they run directly on the BLS result already
# computed for the "Verify Period" button.

# Splits in-transit points by whether they fall in an odd- or even-numbered
# epoch (relative to the detected period) and compares mean depth between
# the two groups. Returns NULL if there isn't enough data spanning multiple
# transits of each parity to make the comparison meaningful.
run_odd_even_test <- function(flux, period_cadences, transit_phase_range, min_epochs_each = 2) {
  fl <- as.vector(flux)
  ok <- is.finite(fl)
  if (sum(ok) < 20 || !is.finite(period_cadences) || period_cadences <= 1) return(NULL)
  
  idx <- which(ok) - 1  # 0-based cadence offset
  vals <- fl[ok]
  epoch <- floor(idx / period_cadences)
  phase <- (idx %% period_cadences) / period_cadences
  in_transit <- phase >= transit_phase_range[1] & phase <= transit_phase_range[2]
  if (sum(in_transit) < 6) return(NULL)
  
  odd_mask  <- in_transit & (epoch %% 2 == 1)
  even_mask <- in_transit & (epoch %% 2 == 0)
  n_odd_epochs  <- length(unique(epoch[odd_mask]))
  n_even_epochs <- length(unique(epoch[even_mask]))
  if (n_odd_epochs < min_epochs_each || n_even_epochs < min_epochs_each) return(NULL)
  
  baseline <- stats::median(vals)
  odd_depth  <- baseline - mean(vals[odd_mask])
  even_depth <- baseline - mean(vals[even_mask])
  odd_sd  <- stats::sd(vals[odd_mask])
  even_sd <- stats::sd(vals[even_mask])
  n_odd  <- sum(odd_mask)
  n_even <- sum(even_mask)
  
  se_diff <- sqrt((odd_sd^2 / n_odd) + (even_sd^2 / n_even))
  diff <- odd_depth - even_depth
  z <- if (is.finite(se_diff) && se_diff > 0) diff / se_diff else NA_real_
  
  list(
    odd_depth = odd_depth, even_depth = even_depth,
    n_odd_transits = n_odd_epochs, n_even_transits = n_even_epochs,
    diff_sigma = z,
    flag_likely_eb = is.finite(z) && abs(z) > 3
  )
}

# Scans phase ~0.5 (opposite the primary transit) for a second, statistically
# significant dip - a background/blended eclipsing binary's secondary
# eclipse. Returns NULL if there isn't enough in- and out-of-transit data to
# compare.
run_secondary_eclipse_check <- function(flux, period_cadences, transit_phase_range, sigma_thresh = 3) {
  fl <- as.vector(flux)
  ok <- is.finite(fl)
  if (sum(ok) < 20 || !is.finite(period_cadences) || period_cadences <= 1) return(NULL)
  
  idx <- which(ok) - 1
  vals <- fl[ok]
  phase <- (idx %% period_cadences) / period_cadences
  
  half_dur <- (transit_phase_range[2] - transit_phase_range[1]) / 2
  primary_center <- mean(transit_phase_range)
  secondary_center <- (primary_center + 0.5) %% 1
  sec_lo <- secondary_center - half_dur
  sec_hi <- secondary_center + half_dur
  
  in_secondary <- if (sec_lo < 0) {
    (phase >= (sec_lo + 1)) | (phase <= sec_hi)
  } else if (sec_hi > 1) {
    (phase >= sec_lo) | (phase <= (sec_hi - 1))
  } else {
    (phase >= sec_lo) & (phase <= sec_hi)
  }
  in_primary <- phase >= transit_phase_range[1] & phase <= transit_phase_range[2]
  out_of_transit <- !in_secondary & !in_primary
  
  if (sum(in_secondary) < 4 || sum(out_of_transit) < 10) return(NULL)
  
  baseline <- mean(vals[out_of_transit])
  base_sd  <- stats::sd(vals[out_of_transit])
  sec_depth <- baseline - mean(vals[in_secondary])
  se <- base_sd / sqrt(sum(in_secondary))
  z <- if (is.finite(se) && se > 0) sec_depth / se else NA_real_
  
  list(
    secondary_depth = sec_depth,
    depth_sigma = z,
    flag_likely_eb = is.finite(z) && z > sigma_thresh
  )
}

# Runs both vetting checks against a run_bls_search()/run_bls_search_auto()
# result. Converts period_days back to cadences (the checks work in cadence
# units) since neither BLS implementation retains per-point epoch numbers.
run_vetting_checks <- function(flux, bls_res, cadence_days = 29.4 / 1440) {
  if (is.null(bls_res)) return(NULL)
  period_cadences <- bls_res$period_days / cadence_days
  list(
    odd_even = run_odd_even_test(flux, period_cadences, bls_res$transit_phase_range),
    secondary_eclipse = run_secondary_eclipse_check(flux, period_cadences, bls_res$transit_phase_range)
  )
}

# Phase-folded verification plot for a run_bls_search() result: flux vs.
# orbital phase (duplicated at phase+1 for visual continuity), with the
# detected in-transit phase range shaded.
build_phase_fold_plotly <- function(res) {
  x <- c(res$folded_phase, res$folded_phase + 1)
  y <- c(res$folded_flux, res$folded_flux)
  rng <- res$transit_phase_range

  p <- plot_ly() %>%
    add_markers(x = x, y = y,
                marker = list(color = "black", size = 4, opacity = 0.5),
                name = "Folded Flux", hoverinfo = "x+y") %>%
    layout(
      title = sprintf("Phase-Folded Light Curve (P = %.3f days)", res$period_days),
      xaxis = list(title = "Orbital Phase", range = c(0, 1.3)),
      yaxis = list(title = "Flux"),
      shapes = list(
        list(type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper",
             x0 = rng[1], x1 = rng[2], y0 = 0, y1 = 1,
             fillcolor = "rgba(220,38,38,0.15)",
             line = list(color = "rgba(220,38,38,0.6)", width = 1)),
        list(type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper",
             x0 = rng[1] + 1, x1 = rng[2] + 1, y0 = 0, y1 = 1,
             fillcolor = "rgba(220,38,38,0.15)",
             line = list(color = "rgba(220,38,38,0.6)", width = 1))
      ),
      showlegend = FALSE
    ) %>%
    config(displaylogo = FALSE)

  return(p)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bandit-style star selector (Thompson Sampling over tagging agreement)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Goal: given the user_star (per-user tags) and test_idx (model-detected
# candidates) tables already queried elsewhere in this file, recommend
# which star most needs another set of eyes on it - i.e. stars that are
# under-tagged (few/no users have looked at them) or where taggers
# disagree with each other.
#
# Why Thompson Sampling rather than a plain epsilon-greedy or UCB1 rule:
#   - Epsilon-greedy explores uniformly at random a fixed fraction of the
#     time, regardless of how much evidence already exists for a star. It
#     can't tell "nobody has tagged this yet" apart from "everybody
#     agrees on this", so it wastes exploration on already-settled stars.
#   - UCB1 is deterministic given the current table state: every session
#     that asks "what should I tag next?" gets back the exact same star.
#     This dashboard is a live, multi-user Shiny app - several people can
#     hit the selector within the same minute - so a deterministic rule
#     would pile everyone onto one star while the rest of the backlog
#     goes untouched.
#   - Thompson Sampling instead treats each star as a Beta-Bernoulli arm
#     and draws a fresh random sample from its posterior every time a
#     recommendation is requested. That randomness spreads concurrent
#     users across several high-priority stars instead of colliding on
#     one, while still concentrating probability mass on stars that most
#     need attention - and it does so without a hand-tuned exploration
#     rate, since "no data yet" already IS maximum uncertainty under a
#     Beta(1, 1) prior.
#
# Arm / reward definition: pulling a star's arm = showing it to a tagger;
# "reward" = 1 if that tagger's windows would disagree with the existing
# consensus, 0 if they'd agree. We don't have that outcome ahead of time,
# so instead of waiting on a live feedback loop we approximate the
# posterior directly, live, from the tags already on file:
#   - >= 2 human taggers: reward posterior is built from the mean
#     pairwise agreement (IoU) across every pair of taggers' saved
#     windows, weighted by how many pairs that mean is based on.
#   - exactly 1 human tagger: compared against the model's own
#     test_idx detection as a (weaker) second opinion.
#   - 0 human taggers: no evidence at all -> uniform Beta(1, 1), i.e.
#     maximum uncertainty, which is exactly what should invite a look.

# Merges a list of c(start, end) windows into a minimal sorted, non
# overlapping set (adjacent/overlapping windows combined).
merge_windows <- function(windows) {
  if (length(windows) == 0) return(list())
  mat <- do.call(rbind, windows)
  mat <- mat[order(mat[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
  merged <- list(as.numeric(mat[1, ]))
  if (nrow(mat) > 1) {
    for (i in 2:nrow(mat)) {
      last <- merged[[length(merged)]]
      if (mat[i, 1] <= last[2] + 1) {
        merged[[length(merged)]][2] <- max(last[2], mat[i, 2])
      } else {
        merged[[length(merged) + 1]] <- as.numeric(mat[i, ])
      }
    }
  }
  merged
}

# Total number of cadence indices covered by a (merged) window set
windows_length <- function(windows) {
  if (length(windows) == 0) return(0)
  sum(vapply(windows, function(w) w[2] - w[1] + 1, numeric(1)))
}

# Total overlap length between two (merged) window sets
windows_intersection_length <- function(a, b) {
  if (length(a) == 0 || length(b) == 0) return(0)
  total <- 0
  for (wa in a) {
    for (wb in b) {
      lo <- max(wa[1], wb[1]); hi <- min(wa[2], wb[2])
      if (hi >= lo) total <- total + (hi - lo + 1)
    }
  }
  total
}

# Jaccard/IoU agreement between two taggers' window sets, in [0, 1].
# Two taggers who both explicitly found nothing (both empty) are defined
# to fully agree; one empty and one non-empty fully disagree.
windows_iou <- function(windows_a, windows_b) {
  a <- merge_windows(windows_a)
  b <- merge_windows(windows_b)
  len_a <- windows_length(a); len_b <- windows_length(b)
  if (len_a == 0 && len_b == 0) return(1)
  inter <- windows_intersection_length(a, b)
  union_len <- len_a + len_b - inter
  if (union_len <= 0) return(1)
  inter / union_len
}

# All human-tagged window sets for a star, one entry per user_id, using
# the same (0,0)-placeholder-drops-to-empty-set convention as
# indices_to_windows() elsewhere in this file.
get_star_human_tag_sets <- function(db_conn, kepler_id) {
  if (!dbExistsTable(db_conn, "user_star")) return(list())
  rows <- dbGetQuery(db_conn, "SELECT user_id, start, end FROM user_star WHERE kepler_id = ?;",
                      params = list(kepler_id))
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(list())
  by_user <- split(rows, rows$user_id)
  lapply(by_user, function(df) indices_to_windows(list(starts = df$start, ends = df$end)))
}

# The model's own detected windows for a star (test_idx), or NULL if the
# table doesn't exist yet or has no rows for this star.
get_star_model_tag_set <- function(db_conn, kepler_id) {
  if (!dbExistsTable(db_conn, "test_idx")) return(NULL)
  rows <- dbGetQuery(db_conn, "SELECT start, end FROM test_idx WHERE id = ?;",
                      params = list(kepler_id))
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(NULL)
  indices_to_windows(list(starts = rows$start, ends = rows$end))
}

# Live Beta-Bernoulli pseudo-counts for one star's "needs more tagging"
# arm, derived from whatever tags currently exist for it.
compute_star_bandit_stats <- function(db_conn, kepler_id) {
  human_sets <- get_star_human_tag_sets(db_conn, kepler_id)
  n_human <- length(human_sets)

  if (n_human >= 2) {
    pairs <- utils::combn(seq_len(n_human), 2, simplify = FALSE)
    ious <- vapply(pairs, function(p) windows_iou(human_sets[[p[1]]], human_sets[[p[2]]]), numeric(1))
    mean_agree <- mean(ious)
    n_pairs <- length(ious)
    tag_source <- "human-human"
  } else if (n_human == 1) {
    model_set <- get_star_model_tag_set(db_conn, kepler_id)
    if (!is.null(model_set)) {
      mean_agree <- windows_iou(human_sets[[1]], model_set)
      n_pairs <- 0.5  # model-vs-human is a weaker signal than human-vs-human
      tag_source <- "human-model"
    } else {
      mean_agree <- 0.5
      n_pairs <- 0
      tag_source <- "single-tagger"
    }
  } else {
    mean_agree <- 0.5
    n_pairs <- 0
    tag_source <- "cold-start"
  }

  list(n_human = n_human, mean_agree = mean_agree, n_pairs = n_pairs, source = tag_source,
       alpha_disagree = 1 + n_pairs * (1 - mean_agree),  # Beta "successes" = disagreement
       alpha_agree = 1 + n_pairs * mean_agree)            # Beta "failures" = agreement
}

# One Thompson-Sampling draw from a star's posterior "needs more tagging"
# probability. Called fresh (new random draw) every time a pick is made.
sample_star_priority <- function(star_stats) {
  stats::rbeta(1, star_stats$alpha_disagree, star_stats$alpha_agree)
}

# Ranks every star in `star_options` (dropdown-format strings, e.g.
# "kplr001718189") by a fresh Thompson-Sampling draw. Returns a data
# frame sorted with the recommended star first.
rank_stars_by_bandit <- function(db_conn, star_options) {
  ids <- vapply(star_options, function(s) as.integer(gsub("^kplr", "", strsplit(s, "_")[[1]][1])), integer(1))
  stats_list <- lapply(ids, function(id) compute_star_bandit_stats(db_conn, id))
  samples <- vapply(stats_list, sample_star_priority, numeric(1))
  out <- data.frame(
    star = star_options,
    kepler_id = ids,
    n_human = vapply(stats_list, `[[`, integer(1), "n_human"),
    mean_agree = vapply(stats_list, `[[`, numeric(1), "mean_agree"),
    source = vapply(stats_list, `[[`, character(1), "source"),
    priority_sample = samples,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  out[order(-out$priority_sample), ]
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Community Tags view helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clusters every human tagger's saved windows for a star into merged
# "regions" of agreement, reusing the same interval-merge machinery as the
# bandit selector above. Input: a named list where each name is a user_id
# and each value is that user's list of c(start, end) windows (e.g. the
# output of get_star_human_tag_sets()). A user who explicitly tagged "no
# transit" contributes an empty window list, so they add no region here,
# but the caller should still count them in the tagger-count denominator
# when reporting "N of M taggers agree" for a region - silence on a region
# is itself information, not a missing vote.
# Returns a data frame with one row per merged region: start, end,
# n_taggers (how many distinct users have a window overlapping it), and
# taggers (a comma-separated list of their names), sorted by start.
build_community_regions <- function(tagger_windows) {
  empty_out <- data.frame(start = integer(0), end = integer(0),
                           n_taggers = integer(0), taggers = character(0),
                           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  rows_list <- lapply(names(tagger_windows), function(tg) {
    ws <- tagger_windows[[tg]]
    if (length(ws) == 0) return(NULL)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(ws, function(w) data.frame(tagger = tg, start = w[1], end = w[2], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  })
  rows <- do.call(rbind, rows_list)
  if (is.null(rows) || nrow(rows) == 0) return(empty_out)
  
  rows <- rows[order(rows$start), ]
  region_id <- integer(nrow(rows))
  region_id[1] <- 1
  cur_region <- 1
  cur_end <- rows$end[1]
  if (nrow(rows) > 1) {
    for (i in 2:nrow(rows)) {
      if (rows$start[i] <= cur_end + 1) {
        region_id[i] <- cur_region
        cur_end <- max(cur_end, rows$end[i])
      } else {
        cur_region <- cur_region + 1
        region_id[i] <- cur_region
        cur_end <- rows$end[i]
      }
    }
  }
  rows$region_id <- region_id
  
  agg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(rows, rows$region_id), function(g) {
    data.frame(
      start = min(g$start), end = max(g$end),
      n_taggers = length(unique(g$tagger)),
      taggers = paste(sort(unique(g$tagger)), collapse = ", "),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
  agg <- agg[order(agg$start), ]
  rownames(agg) <- NULL
  agg
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Crowd-consensus training-data export (closing the loop)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Right now, human tagging only produces a static audit trail: it changes
# what a given user sees, but never feeds back into the model itself. This
# exports two labeled datasets from exactly the tagging data already
# aggregated above, meant to be picked up by an offline retraining/
# fine-tuning script (pipeline.R / main.R - not part of this Shiny app):
#   - "consensus": regions where every human tagger for a star agrees (and
#     at least `min_agreement` of them), i.e. a trustworthy positive label.
#   - "disputed": regions where SOME but not all human taggers for a star
#     flagged something - genuine disagreement, not just an untagged area.
#     These are exactly the hard examples the bandit selector already
#     prioritizes surfacing to human taggers, and make equally good hard
#     examples for fine-tuning (see the "close the loop" discussion this
#     implements).
# Returns list(consensus = data.frame(...), disputed = data.frame(...)),
# both with columns: kepler_id, start, end, n_taggers, n_human, taggers,
# agreement_frac, label.
export_training_labels <- function(db_conn, star_options, min_agreement = 2) {
  ids <- vapply(star_options, function(s) as.integer(gsub("^kplr", "", strsplit(s, "_")[[1]][1])), integer(1))
  
  consensus_rows <- list()
  disputed_rows <- list()
  
  for (id in ids) {
    human_sets <- get_star_human_tag_sets(db_conn, id)
    n_human <- length(human_sets)
    if (n_human == 0) next
    
    regions <- build_community_regions(human_sets)
    if (nrow(regions) == 0) next
    
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(regions))) {
      r <- regions[i, ]
      row <- data.frame(
        kepler_id = id, start = r$start, end = r$end,
        n_taggers = r$n_taggers, n_human = n_human, taggers = r$taggers,
        agreement_frac = r$n_taggers / n_human,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      if (r$n_taggers >= min_agreement && r$n_taggers == n_human) {
        row$label <- "consensus_transit"
        consensus_rows[[length(consensus_rows) + 1]] <- row
      } else if (r$n_taggers >= 1 && r$n_taggers < n_human) {
        row$label <- "disputed"
        disputed_rows[[length(disputed_rows) + 1]] <- row
      }
    }
  }
  
  empty_cols <- c("kepler_id", "start", "end", "n_taggers", "n_human", "taggers", "agreement_frac", "label")
  make_empty <- function() {
    df <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = length(empty_cols), nrow = 0))
    colnames(df) <- empty_cols
    df
  }
  
  consensus_df <- if (length(consensus_rows) > 0) do.call(rbind, consensus_rows) else make_empty()
  disputed_df  <- if (length(disputed_rows)  > 0) do.call(rbind, disputed_rows)  else make_empty()
  rownames(consensus_df) <- NULL
  rownames(disputed_df) <- NULL
  
  list(consensus = consensus_df, disputed = disputed_df)
}

    "CREATE TABLE user_star (",
    "user_id varchar(64), kepler_id int, start int, end int,",
    "label TEXT, flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0, classified_at TEXT);"))
}
if (!dbExistsTable(conn = mydb, name = "user_base")) {
  dbExecute(mydb, paste0(
    "CREATE TABLE user_base (user varchar(64), password_hash varchar(101),",
    "permissions varchar(9), name varchar(64), PRIMARY KEY(user));"))
}
# Additive migration: add new columns to user_star if they don't exist yet.
# SQLite errors when adding an already-existing column; swallow so re-runs are safe.
for (.col_def in c("label TEXT", "flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0", "classified_at TEXT")) {
  tryCatch(dbExecute(mydb, paste0("ALTER TABLE user_star ADD COLUMN ", .col_def, ";")),
           error = function(e) NULL)
}
# Same migration for model-output tables (record_candidates() handles new writes;
# this covers tables that already exist from a previous run before the upgrade).
for (.tbl in c("test_idx", "train_idx")) {
  if (dbExistsTable(mydb, .tbl)) {
    for (.col_def in c("label TEXT", "classified_at TEXT")) {
      tryCatch(dbExecute(mydb, paste0("ALTER TABLE \"", .tbl, "\" ADD COLUMN ", .col_def, ";")),
               error = function(e) NULL)
    }
  }
}
